facts.text: Franklin was founded by Mormon pioneers led by Thomas S. in 1860.
Franklin is named after Apostle Franklin Richards, not Benjamin Franklin, making it the only Franklin County in the U.S. not named after Benjamin Franklin.
The town’s historic buildings, dating back to 1872, include the Lorenzo Hill Hatch House and the Franklin Co‑operative Mercantile Institution, preserved by the Idaho State Historical Society.
Franklin’s early railroad history began in 1878 when the Utah Northern Railroad made the town a division point, giving it a riotous beginning as a terminus.
Parts of the 2004 comedy film Napoleon Dynamite were filmed near Franklin, with chicken‑farm scenes shot on Ritewood Egg Farms.
Travelers along the Pioneer Byway can explore Franklin’s historic properties, offering a comprehensive overview of the region’s history.
